Stooze does his best Alexander Armstrong impression … is Willy Caballero (Argentina) a pointless answer?

Will we see any of Estêvão at the Bridge today? Xabi Alonso has ruled out a January loan exit for the 19-year-old after questions about his limited game time. Estêvão was left on the bench for the Carabao Cup game against Liverpool and has played just 47 minutes in the Premier League so far this season.

“It’s no secret that all players want to be on the pitch,” Alonso said yesterday. “When any of them haven’t had enough minutes because of my decision, I have to take the responsibility for that. articles.title: He was one of the NFL’s most feared runners. Now Larry Johnson fears what football did to his brain
articles.summary: Once among the NFL’s most punishing running backs, Larry Johnson opens up about memory loss, intrusive thoughts and his fears over football’s lasting toll. In his heyday, Larry Johnson was the NFL tailback you’d least want to line up against, the steamroller in pads who had defensive players and…
body: Johnson, who still cuts a fit and formidable figure at age 46, can scarcely recall his glittering career, much less its highlights. “I go up to maybe 2006, 2007,” he tells me. “Anything before or three years after, I really don’t remember.”

When Johnson was thriving as a pro in the mid 2000s, chronic traumatic encephalopathy (CTE), a degenerative brain disease associated with repeated head impacts, was not yet widely recognized as a risk of playing football. The NFL, however, had evidence that head injuries could cause lasting neurological damage, yet spent much of the decade publicly disputing the link as former players sought disability benefits for neurological problems – and were largely denied.

articles.title: Yamashita in command as Hull and Woad fall away in Kuala Lumpur
articles.summary: Defending champion Miyu Yamashita carries a two-stroke lead into Sunday's final round of the LPGA Tour's Maybank Championship after shooting a five-under 67 on Saturday.
body: The 2025 Women's British Open winner and second-round leader had a 54-hole total of 198 to sit 18-under par overall at the Kuala Lumpur Golf and Country Club course.

"It was a very nice round today as well," said Yamashita. "I had a few tricky situations during the round, but I managed to get through them and finish without dropping a shot, so I'm really pleased with that.

China's Yan Liu had the round of the day on Saturday, a 63 which included an eagle, nine birdies and two bogeys, to move into a tie for second place. Pauline Roussin-Bouchard, who led after the first round and shot 67, was level with Yan, who is aiming to keep a steady mindset heading into the final round.

"I just really enjoyed today," said the Chinese player. "I think my swing is in very good position and my putting [was] on fire today. Yeah, really happy for my putter, and I hope tomorrow it's [the] same.

articles.title: Arbeloa: We've made mistakes but Fulham on right path
articles.summary: Having gone winless in your first six games and conceded goals at a rate of almost two a game, there are worse ways to recover than a pair of gritty 1-0 victories.
body: It is still early days in the Alvaro Arbeloa project at Fulham but the optimism that a narrow but entertaining opening-weekend 3-2 defeat to Chelsea had brought from his debut in the dugout had waned with that run, which had left them stranded bottom of the Premier League.

That openness which had initially seemed a welcome tonic from the sometimes pragmatic Marco Silva era had quickly become a problem, with the Cottagers losing 3-2 again - this time to previously winless Crystal Palace - and shipping two late goals to Ipswich earlier this month to lose at Portman Road too.
Something had to change, and after six league games with his players Arbeloa felt he had seen enough to know where that lay.
"We have been learning from our mistakes, and obviously we are a team in a process," he tells Sky Sports. "We are improving, we're working hard and for us to be a very solid team is so important.

articles.title: Shearer on trials of MOTD & the manager's job that never was
articles.summary: Alan Shearer discusses his love of Newcastle, almost continuing his managerial career and swapping the pitch for the commentary box in The Football Interview.
body: Alan Shearer knows that if he wants to preserve his record as the Premier League's all-time record goalscorer, it would be helpful if Erling Haaland moved away from the English top flight.
The former Newcastle United and England striker scored 260 Premier League goals across his 14 years in the league.

Haaland has netted 120 Premier League goals in four-and-a-bit seasons and should he stay with Manchester City - and City stay in the league - it is feasible the Norwegian could surpass Shearer's tally.
However, Shearer acknowledges that if Haaland does not break the record, someone else likely will.

articles.title: Novak pulls three shots clear in Mexico as Hawaiian sensation Akina shines
articles.summary: Andrew Novak caught up to the lead with an eagle and pulled away with three birdies on his last four holes Friday to match his low score on the PGA Tour, a 10-under 61 that gave him a three-shot lead in the Mexico Open.
body: Novak drove the reachable par-four 13th and holed a 12-foot eagle putt as he jostled with Ben Griffin to carry the lead heading into the weekend at Vidanta Vallarta.
But on 15, Griffin drove into the water and had to scramble for a bogey, while Novak holed a birdie putt from just outside 15 feet for a two-shot swing.

Novak closed with a 20-foot birdie putt to finish at 14-under through the opening two rounds, three shots clear of a group of five players that included Griffin (67) and Kihei Akina, the 20-year-old Hawaiian sensation who shot a 64 to post his ninth round of 67 or lower in his last four PGA Tour starts.
Also in the mix were France's Matthieu Pavon (66), Belgium's Adrien Dumont du Chassart (67) and Kensei Hirata of Japan (68).

articles.title: Wales complete Japan double to end WXV on a high
articles.summary: Wales completed a WXV double over Japan with a comfortable 29-5 victory in Kumagaya City.
body: Wing Nel Metcalfe and hooker Moe Nagaoka exchanged tries in the opening 15 minutes before hooker Kelsey Jones and wing Amy Williams added to Wales' first-half haul.
In-form prop Sisilia Tuipulotu crossed after the break before Williams added her second in a rare move from the backs.
Wales were then reduced to 13 players with replacements Keira Bevan and Hannah Dallavalle both shown yellow cards, but dug defensively deep to keep the hosts out in the dying minutes.

Wales finish the Global Series with three wins, their only defeat coming against USA. It marks a complete transformation for Sean Lynn's side, who prior to the South Africa game had gone nine Tests without a win.

articles.title: Sherrock 'happy to overcome hate' after lucrative Littler win
articles.summary: Fallon Sherrock says she has "overcome the hate" after beating Luke Littler to win the second-biggest prize in darts history.
body: The 32-year-old was crowned champion of Netflix's 'Beat Luke Littler' on Friday night after she overcame the double world champion in a one-off leg of 501 to claim a mammoth £501,000 prize.
Only Littler himself has taken more from a single prize pot, the £1million he collected for his second World Championship in January.

This was not Sherrock's first foray into the limelight, as she created history by becoming the first woman to win at the World Championship when she made the third round seven years ago and she went on to break several other barriers in the game.
But her inclusion in the line-up for the TV show attracted criticism given her stature in the game, even if she met the criteria for applicants because she does not hold a PDC Tour Card.

articles.title: Olsen-Baker named Women's World Player of the Year
articles.summary: New Zealand number eight Kaipo Olsen-Baker is named World Rugby's Women's Player of the Year.
body: New Zealand number eight Kaipo Olsen-Baker has been named World Rugby Women's Player of the Year.
The 24-year-old, a powerful ball carrier, beat Canada's DaLeaka Menin and England duo Megan Jones and Zoe Harrison to the award.
Olsen-Baker was a standout performer for a resurgent Black Ferns side, who suffered only one defeat this year under new head coach Whitney Hansen - a 26-19 loss against England in September.
Canada lock Sophie de Goede won the award last year, with England full-back Ellie Kildunne picking it up in 2024.

Although the Saudi city has been the target of deadly attacks in recent weeks, Canelo has arrived ahead of his first fight in 13 months, after he was outpointed by…
body: Against Mbilli, the 36-year-old Canelo faces a stern task; the Cameroonian is the younger man, at 31, and he enters his first title defence with an unbeaten record.

Last time out, on the Canelo vs Crawford undercard, Mbilli fought Lester Martinez to a brutal draw to retain the interim WBC title, but he was later upgraded to regular champion when Crawford retired.
Can Canelo prove that he is still among the best in the world? Or, as he returns from elbow surgery, will he show himself to be in the twilight of his great career? Here’s all you need to know.

articles.title: Central closes regular season with another win. Will playoffs be next?
articles.summary: Two weeks ago nobody gave Central a chance. After Friday night's win over Cumberland, somebody better because it looks like the Knights are heading to the dance.
body: CUMBERLAND – The negativity was everywhere. Instead of sticking through it, some left unwilling to fight the fight. Those who remained had to hear it everywhere, from social media to their own school.

Two weeks ago the Central football team was winless. Today, it looks like the Knights are headed to the postseason. It happened thanks to an incredible comeback in Week 7 which was followed by a dominant defensive performance in a 20-3 win over Cumberland.
“We took this game as a playoff game too, even though it’s a regular season game,” Central’s Richard Bridges said. “This was playoff stakes for us and we had to get it done.”
“It just feels great that we proved them wrong. We shut them up,” Central’s Takari Lee said. “Even going to school, everybody’s saying ‘when are we going to win? When are we going to win?’
